statement: A Hong Kong company is formed by one or more founder members signing the articles of association and delivering to the Registrar of Companies for registration an incorporation form in the specified form (Form NNC1 for a company limited by shares) together with a copy of the articles, and on registering them the Registrar must issue a certificate of incorporation certifying that the company is incorporated under the Companies Ordinance; the Companies Registry's one-stop service files the Notice to Business Registration Office (IRBR1) with the same submission.
caveat: Section 67 requires formation for a lawful purpose, section 70 requires a statement of compliance in the incorporation form, and section 73 fixes corporate existence from the date of incorporation stated in the certificate. Electronic filing runs through the Registry's e-Services Portal; hard-copy delivery remains available.
